title: The integral stratum bound
statement:
In the situation of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion],

$$
\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)=0\quad(q>\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2),
$$

Ext taken in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Use the standing scheme and coefficient setting of the unit, and write $R_Y=\mathcal O_{E,Y}$ and $A_{n,Y}=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$ for every scheme $Y$, with $n\geq1$. Put $Q=a_!L_0$, $N=b_!M_0$, and $\overline N_n=b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$. In the integral category let $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_{R_X\to A_{n,X}}\overline N_n$. Clause (4) of [sk-lem-integral-models], applied separately to $a,L_0$ and to $b,M_0$, identifies $Q\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X}$ with $a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$ and the underlying integral reduction of $N$ with $N_n$. Clauses (2) and (4) also make $N$ derived complete. Hence [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] gives $N\simeq R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}N_n$, with the canonical quotient transitions. All occurrences of a finite-coefficient object in the integral category here and below mean termwise restriction of scalars.

source.place: Lattices, derived reductions of the extensions by zero; Integral targets, derived completeness of the target

proof.text: In the integral coefficient category define $T(K)=L_0^\vee\otimes_{R_S}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, $F=T(N)$ and $F_n=T(N_n)$. The dual $L_0^\vee$ is finite locally free: on a trivialization of $L_0$ it is the dual finite free module, and the inverse transpose transition matrices glue these local duals. By [sk-lem-formal-closed-support-ii], both $u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z$ and tensoring with this dual carry sequential derived-limit triangles to the corresponding triangles of their image sequences. Apply these two assertions successively to Step 1 to obtain $F\simeq R\varprojlim_nF_n$ in $D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},R_S)$. This defines $F_n$ using integral support; no change-of-coefficient assertion about derived support is being presumed.

source.place: Integral targets, applying the limit-preserving closed-support and finite locally free tensor functors

proof.text: Clause (2) of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support] with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(Q,N)\simeq R\Gamma(S,F)$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(Q,N_n)\simeq R\Gamma(S,F_n)$. Set $B_n=R\Gamma(S,F_n)$, forgetting the coefficient action so that $B_n\in D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Apply [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] to the ringed site $(S_{\mathrm{proét}},R_S)$, its terminal object $S$, and the tower of Step 2; choose a universe in which this site is small and reindex $n=m+1$ to use $m\geq0$. It gives $R\Gamma(S,F)\simeq R\varprojlim_nB_n$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. The underlying complexes compute the same cohomology groups. Thus $\Ext^q_{R_X}(Q,N)=H^q(R\varprojlim_nB_n)$ and $H^q(B_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(Q,N_n[q])$, by the definitions of derived Hom and Ext.

source.place: Integral targets, support-Hom formula and commuting derived global sections with the derived limit; Stacks Tag 0D6K, label lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim

proof.text:
For each $n$, apply the derived extension/termwise restriction adjunction stated in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] to the quotient morphism of condensed rings $\underline{\mathcal O_E}\to\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. Together with the source reduction from [sk-lem-integral-models], this gives, for every integer $q$,
$$H^q(B_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(Q,\operatorname{Res}\overline N_n[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_{n,X})}(Q\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X},\overline N_n[q])=\Ext^q_{A_{n,X}}\bigl(a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n),b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)\bigr).$$
The adjunction is for arbitrary coefficient morphisms; in particular it requires no flatness of $R_X\to A_{n,X}$. It compares groups in the two different module categories rather than identifying those categories.

source.place: Integral targets, comparison with the torsion reductions, expanded via the coefficient-change adjunction; coefficient-change section, displayed derived extension and its adjunction

proof.text:
Use clause (2) of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support] over the admissible finite ring $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$ to express the last group of Step 4 as
$$H^qR\Gamma\bigl(S,(L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n)\otimes_{A_{n,S}}u^*R\underline\Gamma_{Z,A_n}\,b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)\bigr).$$
Indeed $(L_0/\pi_E^n)^\vee=L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n$: in a local finite basis both evaluation pairings are the dot product over $A_n$, and their inverse transpose transition matrices agree, so these identifications glue. The ring $A_n$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, and the reduced source is finite locally free, as required by the support formula. Clause (2) of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion] now gives $H^q(B_n)=0$ for $q>c$, uniformly in $n$, where $c=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+1$. In particular the torsion bound is applied in its own coefficient category.

source.place: Integral targets, the assertion that the reductions have the torsion stratum bound; Torsion targets, last display

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] to the tower $B_n$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ from Step 3. It gives
$$0\longrightarrow R^1\varprojlim_nH^{q-1}(B_n)\longrightarrow H^q(R\varprojlim_nB_n)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_nH^q(B_n)\longrightarrow0.$$
For $q>c+1$, both $q>c$ and $q-1>c$, so Step 5 makes each of the two towers in the end terms the zero tower. Their limit and first derived limit are zero (the zero object has the zero injective resolution), hence the middle group is zero by exactness. Step 3 identifies that group with $\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)$. Since $c+1=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$, this is precisely the claimed bound. No surjectivity or Mittag-Leffler assumption on the cohomology towers is used. If a cohomological dimension is infinite the claimed range is empty, so only the finite-bound case needs this computation.

source.place: Integral targets, final Milnor argument; Stacks Tag 07KY, label lemma-break-long-exact-sequence

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N3-a93ee379a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, its unit, the blueprint statement and proof (integral, torsion, _section) and the statement of every cited node. The statement is the blueprint's verbatim; Ext is in D(X_proet, R_X = p_X^*O_E), the same coefficient ring as in all cited nodes. Step 1: sk-lem-integral-models (4), applied to (a,L_0) and (b,M_0), gives the reductions; clause (2) gives derived completeness, so N = Rlim N_n by sk-def-pe-derived-completion. The words 'canonical transitions' are only identified object by object, but this is harmless because the Milnor step needs only that each H^q(B_n) vanishes. Step 2: sk-lem-formal-closed-support-ii with Lambda = O_E gives F = Rlim F_n in the integral category. Step 3: sk-lem-formal-closed-support (2) plus lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit (Stacks 0D6K) gives RHom(Q,N) = Rlim B_n in D(Ab). Step 4: the coefficient-change adjunction (derived extension left adjoint to Res) for O_E -> O_E/pi^n needs no flatness and does not identify the categories; it avoids the blueprint's tacit identification of integral and A_n-coefficient RGamma_Z. Step 5: support formula (2) over the admissible A_n, then torsion clause (2) in its own category, gives H^q(B_n)=0 for q>c. Step 6: the Milnor sequence in D(Ab) (07KY/08TB) gives vanishing for q>c+1, which is exactly the claimed +2. Edge cases checked: Spec of an algebraically closed field (bound q>2, true), empty strata, n=1, infinite cohomological dimension.
